steps.scene: You're driving along when a red warning light you don't recognise comes on on the dashboard.

options.text: Ignore it while the car still seems to drive normally
Check out the problem as soon as you safely can
Stop at once, wherever you are

question.explanation: A warning light can mean the car isn't safe to drive. Pull over safely and check the handbook — get help if you're unsure.

steps.title: Tyre tread: the legal limit
steps.body: Car tyres need at least 1.6 mm of tread across the central three-quarters, all the way round — with no deep cuts or bulges.

question.prompt: What's the legal minimum tread depth for car tyres?

options.text: 1 mm
Any tread is legal as long as the tyre isn't bald
1.6 mm

question.explanation: 1.6 mm is the legal floor, not a safe target. Grip in the wet falls away well before then.

a.label: Under-inflated
a.body: Longer stopping distances, poorer handling and more fuel used.

b.label: Checked cold
b.body: Driving warms tyres and raises the reading. Check before you set off.

question.prompt: When should you check your tyre pressures?

options.text: When the tyres are cold
After a long drive, once the tyres have warmed up
Only when the car is serviced

question.explanation: Compare the cold reading with the figure in the handbook, and adjust it for a heavy load if the handbook says so.

steps.scene: Every time you brake, the car pulls towards the left.

options.text: Nothing — it's just the camber of the road
Pump the brakes to even them out
Have the brakes checked as soon as possible

question.explanation: Brakes pulling to one side usually means a fault. It can make you swerve in an emergency stop.

steps.title: Set your head restraint
steps.body: A properly adjusted head restraint cuts the risk of neck injury in a crash. Set it before you drive, close to the back of your head.

question.prompt: What's the main reason to adjust your head restraint properly?

options.text: To make long journeys more comfortable
To help you avoid neck injury
To stop you nodding off at the wheel

question.explanation: In a crash your head is thrown forwards, then back. A well-set restraint stops it snapping backwards.

steps.wrongBelief: With driver-assist systems switched on, the car is doing the driving.

question.prompt: Your car has lane-keep assist and adaptive cruise control switched on. Who's in control?

options.text: You are — the systems only help
The car, while the systems are switched on
The systems, until they sound a warning

question.explanation: Driver-assist systems are there to make driving safer. They can't see everything, so you stay responsible.

steps.repairNote: Driver-assist systems support you. You must stay alert and in control of the car at all times.

steps.scene: You're popping into a shop for two minutes. You've parked right outside the door.

question.prompt: What should you do with the car?

options.text: Leave the engine running — you'll be straight back
Switch off, take the key and lock it
Leave the key in so you can keep an eye on it

question.explanation: Cars are stolen in seconds. Leaving the key in can also invalidate your insurance.
